rationale: The Court is likely to adopt a narrow, clear-statement-driven reading: § 544(b)(1) is derivative and requires an actual creditor with a viable nonbankruptcy cause of action against the same transferee, and § 106(a) waives immunity only for properly constituted § 544 actions rather than rewriting that predicate. The Chief is best positioned to hold the coalition together, while Justice Sotomayor is the most likely separate writer to argue that the 1994 § 106(a) amendment makes the waiver effective even when sovereign immunity would block any outside-bankruptcy creditor suit.
